ai-building-workspace.name: AI Building Workspace
ai-building-workspace.tagline: Understand the drawing. Turn the building into data.
ai-building-workspace.summary: A workspace that reads DXF drawings, computes room boundaries and areas, and turns them into a 3D building model you can check against the drawings. We're testing it on real green-remodeling drawings.
ai-building-workspace.coverAlt: Axonometric of the 3D building model AI Building Workspace built from the drawings, with the unconfirmed roof in orange
why: Most building information still lives as lines and text on drawings. Every time someone needs an area or a quantity, a person has to read the drawing again and copy numbers into a spreadsheet, and later it is hard to tell where those numbers came from.
AI Building Workspace turns a single drawing into building data you can verify. AI reads the drawing, a person reviews the result, and every figure keeps its evidence.

case.title: Tested on real drawings
case.intro: We fed in one full set of green-remodeling drawings (DXF) for a small public health clinic. The ground floor is the clinic; the upper floor is staff housing. Client and architect details are removed; only the drawing linework is redrawn.

plan.title: Original ground-floor plan
plan.caption: Redrawn from the DXF's wall, opening and dimension layers only. Scale 1:100, overall 10,500 × 9,800 mm.

rooms.title: Computed room boundaries
rooms.caption: Closed regions are found from wall and opening lines and labelled with the room names in the drawing. Two areas with no partition line are grouped and flagged for boundary review.

model.title: 3D model built from the drawings
model.caption: Turn it around right in the browser. Take floors off and tap a room to see the area computed from the drawings, or lay the drawn plan on the floor to check it against the model. The roof, which the drawings alone can't settle, is an unconfirmed element.

interior1.title: Ground floor inside · clinic
interior1.caption: The model is cut 1.4 m above the floor and viewed from above. Each room's floor-finish grid lines up with the room layout in the drawings; labels sit at the centre of the room boundaries computed from the drawing layers.

interior2.title: Upper floor inside · staff housing
interior2.caption: The upper floor cut the same way. The living room and kitchen/dining are open to each other, so they are computed as one area. Balconies are open to the outside and are not counted as rooms.

materials.title: Finishes from the drawings
materials.intro: The finishes noted on the construction drawings are applied to the same model and rendered. Colours and textures are approximations of each finish type, not specific product specifications.

images.exterior: Exterior · stucco walls and zinc roof
images.cutaway: Ground floor · vinyl deco tile floors, painted walls

wall.finish: 100 mm PF board external insulation + stucco

window.finish: Double sliding PVC windows · 24 mm tinted low-E double glazing

floor1.finish: Heavy-traffic vinyl deco tile (porcelain tile in the toilet)

wall1.finish: Water-based paint · painted gypsum board (ceramic wall tile and SMC ceiling in the toilet)

wall2.finish: Wallpaper · gypsum board with ceiling paper

materials.note: Furniture and light fittings are not in the drawings, so none were added. Interior lights are placed approximately at the centre of each room's ceiling.

compare.title: Elevation overlay
compare.caption: The drawn front elevation and the model's front view share the same scale and origin. Drag the slider or switch to overlay to see how closely the lines match.

takeoff.title: Quantity takeoff from the drawings
takeoff.intro: Perimeter (L), floor area (A) and wall area (WA) are measured from the room boundaries, then the finishes noted on the drawings are attached to produce quantities per material. Window and door areas taken from the 3D model are deducted from the walls. Amounts use example unit prices.

1f.title: Quantity markup drawing · ground floor
1f.caption: Colours show floor finishes; red lines are windows and doors deducted from wall area. Orange dashes mark zones with no partition line that need boundary review.

2f.title: Quantity markup drawing · upper floor
2f.caption: Veranda boundaries are closed with the parapet (PAR) lines; the part of the boundary not touching the building is estimated as railing length.

takeoff.basis: L perimeter · A floor area · WA = L × ceiling height {height} m − window/door area (interior doors deducted on both sides)
takeoff.materialsTitle: Quantities and example amounts by material
takeoff.priceNote: * Unit prices are examples assuming typical market rates including materials and labour; they are not a real estimate. The upper-floor stairwell (unnamed in the drawings) and demolition, MEP and electrical works are not included.

areas.note: The next step is to confirm whether the noted figure uses wall centrelines or includes an allowance. Rather than forcing the numbers to match, we keep a record of where the gap comes from.

findings.title: What matched and what didn't yet
confirmed: Ground-floor overall dimensions and room zones match the drawn plan.
Front windows, entrance door and the gable outline line up with the drawn elevation.
The model's floor-finish zones on each floor line up with the room layout in the drawings.
open: The roof form can't be settled from the front elevation alone and stays unconfirmed; it needs checking against the roof plan.
The balcony railing, accessible ramp and entrance steps are not in the model yet.
Three areas with no partition line (clinic/dispensary, stairwell/boiler room, upper-floor living/kitchen) need their boundaries confirmed by a person.
The upper-floor stairwell has no room name or closed boundary in the drawings, so it is missing from the quantities.
There is a gap between the works area noted on the drawing and the computed area.
